name: DividedSplitting.norm_schur_inv_cols_le_weylGauge
summary: Insert the diagonal matrix with M⁻¹ on S and 1 elsewhere: the product of the inverse columns with K and with diag(M on S) is integral, so its Schur matrix has norm ≤ 1, and the Schur matrix of the diagonal costs the power of |M|_p.

steps.claim: Lift K to k ∈ K₀ (reductionK₀ is surjective).
Write h = k⁻¹·h' and use that the Weyl gauge is invariant under K₀ (weylGauge_mul at the local level).
steps.lean: obtain ⟨h, rfl⟩ := mul_right_surjective k⁻¹.1 h; rw [weylGauge_mul h (Kf_le_localLevel k⁻¹.2)]

steps.claim: Unfold the gauge and the Weyl representation; move the inclusion matrices through the products (e).
steps.lean: simp_all [weylGauge, weylRep, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, mul_inclMatrix, submatrix_mul (e₂ := id)]

steps.claim: Bound the vector by the norm of S_κ(diag(M⁻¹ on S, 1)) times S_κ of the integral matrix (columns f of (gγ)⁻¹)·k·diag(M on S, 1), whose Schur matrix has norm ≤ 1 (norm_schur_mulVec_le, entries of norm ≤ 1 after the weight embedding: norm_adeleExtension_le_one); integrality of the entries in S follows from their vanishing modulo M (reduction_levelModulus_eq_zero_iff, the goal of step 7).
steps.lean:
grw [← norm_mulVec_le (M := schur κ fun _ ↦ diagonal (S.piecewise M⁻¹ 1)), ←
    norm_schur_mulVec_le hl.1 fun τ i j ↦ norm_adeleExtension_le_one (weightEmbedding ιₚ τ)
    (reduction_levelModulus_eq_zero_iff.1 (?_ : (O.levelModulus 1 false).reduction ((∑ c,
    ⟨_, L.integral i (f c)⟩ * ⟨_, k.2.isIntMatrix c j⟩) * ite (j ∈ S) ↑M 1) = 0))]

steps.claim: The two Schur matrices multiply to that of the product (HasColumnsBelow.schur_mul_schur under hl), which is the original matrix; compare entrywise.
steps.lean:
erw [mulVec_mulVec, mulVec_mulVec, hl.schur_mul_schur,
    hl.schur_mul_schur]; congr! 5; ext; erw [mul_apply, mul_apply]

steps.claim: Split the cases j ∈ S or not of the diagonal entry.
For j ∈ S the entry Σ_c (ϖγ⁻¹)_{ic}·k_{cj} vanishes modulo M (from hS: ϖ̄·(G_f·K)_{ij} = 0 modulo M² gives the entry ≡ 0 modulo M), using the definition of reducedInverse.
steps.lean:
simp_all [mul_apply, DividedLattice.reducedInverse, reductionK₀, ← map_mul, ← map_sum,
    reduction_levelModulus_eq_zero_iff, sq, mul_assoc]

steps.claim: The Schur matrix of a diagonal matrix is diagonal with entries the products of powers (schur_diagonal).
steps.lean:
all_goals simp +contextual [schur_diagonal, piecewise, diagonal_apply, apply_ite (GE.ge _),
    apply_ite, prod_pow_eq_pow_sum, ← inv_pow, mul_assoc, ← mul_sum]

steps.claim: Each diagonal entry is at most |M|_p^{−(...)} since |M|_p ≤ 1.
steps.lean: intro i; gcongr; simp [one_le_inv₀, NeZero.ne, norm_natCast_le_one]

steps.claim: The exponent is bounded by the tableau weights (sum_tableauWeight_le) and the diagram weights, giving |S|·Σ_{i<|l|} κ(τ, i) at each τ.
